papers.title: A multi-scale forecasting framework to prioritize clinically-relevant antibiotic resistance alleles
papers.abstract: Established in vitro measures for the emergence of antimicrobial resistance, a critical global threat, can fail to predict which in vitro discovered mutations will dominate in the real world following widespread antibiotic use. Here, we introduce a multi-scale computational framework integrating genetic constraints and population pharmacokinetics and apply it to explain resistance allele success in Acinetobacter baumannii for the historic case of resistance to the fluoroquinolone antibiotic ciprofloxacin. By coupling intrinsic nucleotide substitution likelihoods with continuous-time stochastic modeling under fluctuating drug exposures, our framework clearly prioritizes the most common real world gyrA fluoroquinolone resistance allele S81L over rarer alleles, reflecting its clinical success. While gyrA serves as a proof-of-concept case study for direct, active-site drug-target interactions where the target space is constrained, we observe that the nucleotide substitution likelihoods are not explaining allele success in resistance-determining genes pmrB and adeS. Furthermore, "virtual twin" cohort simulations reveal that restricted drug penetration or compromised immunity expands selective windows, rescuing rare, low-fitness alleles. This advances our understanding of prospective, model-informed risk prediction during antibiotic development.

papers.title: Klebsiella taiwanensis sp. nov., and Pseudomonas ficus sp. nov., novel taxa isolated from figs (Ficus)
papers.abstract: Two bacterial strains, WOUb02T and WOUb67T, were isolated from fresh figs (Ficus spp.) collected from the island of Taiwan. Cells of WOUb02T and WOUb67T were Gram-stain-negative rods. Strain WOUb02T was non-motile, whereas WOUb67T exhibited motility. Physiologically, both strains grew optimally at 0.5% (w/v) NaCl and pH 8.0; WOUb02T grew optimally at 37{degrees}C, whereas WOUb67T grew optimally at 30{degrees}C. Based on 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity, the closest relatives to strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T were Klebsiella terrigena ATCC 33257T (98.2%) and Pseudomonas putida NBRC 14164T (99.9%) respectively. Subsequent phylogenetic analysis based on 16S rRNA gene sequences revealed that strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T formed distinct lineages within the genera Klebsiella and Pseudomonas, respectively. Further genomic analyses revealed that WOUb02T and WOUb67T shared average nucleotide identity and digital DNA-DNA hybridization values <95.0% and <70.0%, below the currently accepted thresholds for species-level delineation. Based on phenotypic and genotypic data, strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T could be distinguished from other species with validly published names and are considered to represent novel species in the genera Klebsiella and Pseudomonas, respectively, for which the names Klebsiella taiwanensis sp. nov., and Pseudomonas ficus sp. nov., are proposed. The type strains are WOUb02T (=NRRL-B 65719T =CCUG 77855T) and WOUb67T (=NRRL-B 65720T =CCUG 77856T).

papers.title: Oral microbiome and DNA virome profiling in pigs reveals age-associated dynamics and extracellular recovery of Streptococcus suis-associated phage lineages
papers.abstract: The pig oral cavity is a critical interface for microbial transmission and herd health monitoring, yet its microbiome and virome remains poorly characterised. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of oral fluids from pigs across 15 commercial farms in Ireland, using paired bulk and virus-like particles (VLP) enrichment to capture comprehensive microbial and DNA virome diversity. Microbial communities shifted progressively with age, with early post-weaning animals enriched in environmental genera such as Pseudomonas and Staphylococcus and later stages dominated by lactic acid bacteria and anaerobes. Only 20.6% of vOTUs could be assigned to a known genus, with the most abundant being Astrithrvirus, which increased with age. Both microbiome and DNA virome exhibited predictable, coordinated age-associated succession with strong cross-domain coupling supported by virus-host networks. Functional profiling of the microbiome revealed that predicted carbohydrate substrates tracked the dietary transitions, while accessory viral functions partitioned by lifestyle and host. The early post-weaning stage was characterised by high abundance of viral integration and excision functions, as well as elevated resistome diversity that was almost exclusively of prokaryotic origin rather than viral. Importantly, 26 of the 25,223 vOTUs identified were predicted to target Streptococcus suis, providing the first metagenomic catalogue of such phages from pig oral environments. These findings expand our understanding of oral microbiome-virome dynamics and establish a framework for integrated microbiome and viromics approaches that could enable therapeutic phage discovery and inform microbiome-targeted interventions in pig production systems.

papers.title: ViruDB: An Assay-Aware Molecular Database and Endpoint-Adaptive Multimodal Learning Framework for Antibiofilm, Quorum-Sensing Inhibition, and Antivirulence Research
papers.abstract: Antibiofilm and quorum-sensing inhibitory molecules have become increasingly attractive candidates to complement traditional antibacterial approaches, but the experimental evidence ranges from heterogeneous assays, organisms, methods of activity measurement, and chemical representation. We created ViruDB, a molecular evidence resource that is assay-aware, and tested an endpoint-adaptive multimodal learning framework for quantitative activity prediction. Curated collection of 8765 experimental evidence records for 3563 unique molecules: 2,959 quantitative observations, of which 2,345 were antibiofilm, 569 were quorum-sensing inhibition [QSI], and 45 were antivirulence. Molecular representations included 217 2D descriptors from RDKit, 2,048-bit ECFP4 fingerprints, molecular graphs, and some information about the biological context. A molecule- and scaffold-disjoint primary partition was used, which resulted in 2,339 observations in the training set, 265 observations in the validation set and 355 observations in the independent test set. ViruFusion-TaskExpert-MTL and an endpoint specific combination with classical regressors were selected by validation. The final predictor yielded an RMSE value of 0.5460 and an R2 of 0.4816 on the antibiofilm activity dataset (n=286) and an RMSE value of 0.5744 and an R2 of 0.4082 on the QSI dataset (n=67) in the reported frozen independent evaluation. Exploratory anti-virulence regression (n=2 test observations). The results validate quantitative, endpoint based prioritization under chemical novelty and highlight the significance of assay provenance, assay leakage control and external biological assay validation.

papers.title: Integrative structural biology of a giant marine virus reveals architectural and functional complexity beyond icosahedral symmetry
papers.abstract: Knowledge of giant virus diversity has expanded rapidly; however, isolated representatives remain scarce, and few have been examined at high resolution. Here, we characterized haptophyte-infecting Prymnesium kappa virus RF02 (PkV-RF02) using integrative structural biology. The ~3 [A] resolution structure obtained by block-based cryo-electron microscopy reconstruction shows a pseudoT=219 icosahedral shell built from over 20 different proteins and approximately 10,000 polypeptides, a multi-layered stabilization network reinforced by 20,000 disulphide bridges, two penton variants evenly distributed in the capsid, and a protein channel crossing the internal membrane. Cross-linking mass spectrometry defines the intricate capsid-membrane-core interaction network, which includes a second major capsid protein, a third penton variant, and multiple biochemical functions packaged within the virion. Phospho- and glycoproteomics reveal widespread post-translational modifications, with approximately 50% of proteins phosphorylated and uncommon methyl-N-acetylated viosamine glycans. This study provides a comprehensive structural and interaction map that highlights organizational and functional innovations underlying giant virus assembly.

papers.title: Infant formula composition is linked to distinct patterns of early gut colonization
papers.abstract: Early-life nutrition shapes the gut microbiota and can have long-term health implications. While infant formula feeding is widespread, it remains unclear how variations in its nutritional components shape microbiome colonization. Here, we reconstructed 62 components across the 17 infant formulas consumed during the first three months of life in 240 exclusively formula-fed infants in the Lifelines-NEXT birth cohort. Formula composition varied widely and several micronutrients, including vitamin E and iodine, were associated with species richness. Components were also associated with species-level colonization patterns. Higher iron content was associated with reduced Bifidobacterium breve and Bifidobacterium bifidum and increased Clostridium paraputrificum. Follow-up in vitro growth assays on infant-derived stool isolates showed that Bifidobacterium breve and Bifidobacterium bifidum tolerated iron limitation, while C. paraputrificum did not, consistent with the association signals. These findings show that infant formulas are not all alike and differences in component concentration affect microbiome colonization in early-life.

papers.title: DRP1 Orchestrates RNA Virus Permissiveness Through Metabolic Reprogramming Independent of Mitochondrial Dynamics
papers.abstract: Viruses reprogram host metabolism and mitochondrial dynamics to support replication, yet how these processes govern viral permissiveness remains unclear. Using SARS-CoV-2 alongside other RNA viruses JEV, VSV, and HCV, we identify DRP1 as a central determinant of the virus-permissive cellular state beyond mitochondrial fission. While RNA viruses induce pronounced mitochondrial fragmentation linked to enhanced permissiveness, MFN1 conferred potent antiviral protection independent of type I interferon. Targeting DRP1-associated functions pharmacologically suppresses viral replication, accompanied by decreased glycolysis and enhanced oxidative metabolism. Remarkably, genetic depletion of DRP1 itself potently restricts viral replication in both wild-type and MFN1-deficient cells despite persistent mitochondrial fragmentation in the latter, demonstrating that MFN1 and mitochondrial elongation are dispensable for antiviral restriction. Together, these findings identify DRP1 as a key regulator of viral permissiveness operating beyond mitochondrial morphology. By uncoupling mitochondrial morphology from antiviral regulation, our study highlights DRP1-associated pathways as promising targets for host-directed antiviral strategies.

papers.title: The identification of 110 novel Mycobacterium species within 57,974 UK Health Security Agency clinical samples
papers.abstract: Non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTMs) are a large diverse group of opportunistic pathogens. The accurate identification of species within this genus is vital as pathogenicity, epidemiology, and treatment differ substantially between taxa. Whole-genome sequencing has improved taxonomic resolution, however current reference databases are likely incomplete. We analysed 53,170 high-quality mycobacterial genomes from 57,974 UK Health Security Agency samples collected between 2010 and 2025, a collection more than four times larger than the 12,726 mycobacterial genomes represented in GTDB release r232. High-quality isolates were assigned by average nucleotide identity (ANI) to recognised species within the Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB) using a 95% ANI threshold. Isolates that fell below this threshold were clustered using a minimal dominating set approach to identify genomically coherent groups consistent with being candidate novel species. Phylogenetic analysis of all Mycobacterium species was used to place the observed UK diversity in a global context and assess the ecological structure within the genus. Of the 850 Mycobacterial species-level reference genomes in GTDB, 204 GTDB references received at least one provisional assignment. We identified 586 (1.1%) high-quality isolates that could not be assigned to any GTDB species. Genomic clustering identified 110 additional candidate species-level references, expanding the reference set from 850 to 960 (12.9%). These candidate species were broadly distributed across the phylogeny. Within the Mycobacterium genus we found strong evidence that phylogenetic structure is associated with human (Fritz and Purvis D = 0.10, p<0.001) and environmental sources (D = 0.34, p<0.001). Together, existing and novel reference genomes resolved the UKHSA collection into 275 species-level clusters, of which 110 (40.0%) were not represented by existing GTDB references. Furthermore, source associations differed substantially between phylogenetic clades ({chi}{superscript 2} = 364 for human and {chi}{superscript 2} = 258 for environmental association; both p<0.001). Rarefaction analysis of the 275 species observed in UKHSA clinical samples did not plateau, with Chao1 estimation suggesting that additional sampling may reveal further novel species (Chao1 = 461). This study provides a comprehensive analysis of genomic NTM diversity within a large national surveillance collection. Our findings suggest that NTM diversity remains incompletely characterised, and supports the value of continued surveillance and curation to improve bacterial reference databases.

papers.title: Cross-species dissemination of diverse plasmid lineages and mobile resistance modules shapes carbapenemase co-production in Chilean Enterobacterales
papers.abstract: Carbapenemase co-production among Enterobacterales is an emerging clinical challenge, yet the relative contributions of clonal expansion, cross-species plasmid dissemination, and movement of resistance modules remain unclear. We integrated national surveillance data with plasmid-resolved hybrid genomes to investigate these processes in Chile. Among 414 isolates carrying at least two carbapenemase families referred during 2018-2024, annual numbers increased markedly alongside broader taxonomic and geographic representation. Thirty isolates were selected to span variation in year, species, region, and carbapenemase profile. These represented 11 species from six genera and contained 149 complete plasmids, 57 of which carried carbapenemase genes. Of 63 carbapenemase gene copies, 62 were plasmid-borne, and 55 of the 57 carbapenemase-carrying plasmids were predicted to be conjugative or mobilizable. Complementary plasmid typing, whole-sequence clustering, structural comparisons, and pan-plasmidome analysis identified three recurrent lineages: IncX3/blaNDM-7, IncN/blaKPC-2, and IncHI2A/blaVIM-1. Their occurrence across multiple species and sequence types supported cross-species dissemination, while numerous minor groups and singletons revealed a broader repertoire of plasmid architectures and accessory genes. Related backbones carried variable resistance regions, and equivalent class 1 integrons and transposon-associated platforms occurred in otherwise unrelated plasmids, indicating modular redistribution of carbapenemase genes. In selected isolates, co-resident plasmids created resistance redundancy, brought recurrent carbapenemase plasmid lineages together, or coupled resistance and virulence within the same cell. Thus, co-production did not arise through a single route: bacterial clones, plasmids shared across species, and mobile resistance modules each contributed to its emergence. Complete plasmid resolution is essential to distinguish these processes and track their dissemination.

papers.title: Hyphosphere Hunting Grounds: Fungal Hyphae Guide a Protist Predator to its Bacterial Prey
papers.abstract: Interactions between microeukaryotes mediated by prokaryotic intermediaries remain poorly understood. Here, we show that the hyphae of a plant pathogen guide bacterivorous protists into bacterial habitats, transforming a fungal dispersal route into a potential hunting ground. Although fungal hyphae are established dispersal corridors for bacteria, their capacity to guide individual protist cells remains largely unexplored. Time-lapse imaging of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. vasinfectum Race 4 revealed bacteria and the flagellate Paracercomonas sp. moving bidirectionally along hyphae with significant axial alignment, despite contrasting motility regimes: rapid, superdiffusive bacterial movement and slower, subdiffusive protist movement. The ciliate Paracolpoda steinii also exhibited directional alignment along an inert glass rod, demonstrating that physical geometry can bias protist movement independently of fungal-specific cues. Across successive generational culturing of hyphal-baits, protist communities converged reproducibly toward Paracolpoda dominance, whereas bacterial assembly was largely stochastic, revealing contrasting assembly processes within the same habitat. In a dual-microcosm assay, fungal bridges enabled bacteria and protists to cross a 3 mm air gap, while the presence of P. steinii reduced bacterial arrival approximately 8-fold, consistent with predator-associated filtering. Together, these findings extend the fungal-highway concept beyond microbial transport, identifying pathogenic fungal hyphae as multi-kingdom ecological corridors where physical guidance, community assembly and predator-associated effects on dispersal intersect.

papers.title: Viral genetic variation programs divergent neuroimmune states during rabies infection
papers.abstract: Viral burden does not necessarily predict the extent or composition of the host immune response, reflecting the complexity of virus - host interactions. Rabies virus (RABV) provides a powerful model to investigate this question because genetically distinct RABVs differ in replication, immune evasion, and neuroimmune activation. Here, we performed integrated temporal proteomic and spatial imaging analyses of recombinant RABV, including pathogenic, attenuated, and a newly generated interferon-sensitive variant with disrupted phosphoprotein antagonistic activity. Following intracerebral infection of mice, viruses established distinct neuroimmune states that diverged over time in antiviral signaling, complement activation, and immune response. Notably, the pathogenic field viruses rDogA and rFox both exhibited substantial viral accumulation, but elicited markedly different central nervous system (CNS) responses, with rDogA inducing limited host immune engagement, whereas rFox triggered early and broad antiviral, complement, and immune recruitment programs. Disruption of phosphoprotein-mediated interferon antagonism in rDogA enhanced interferon-stimulated gene expression and antiviral effectors, restricting viral accumulation without inducing broad neuroimmune remodeling. Conversely, the attenuated glycoprotein-modified rSAD GASGAS elicited strong complement activation and T cell recruitment with little detectable viral levels, revealing a highly immunogenic neuroimmune state. Spatial profiling further identified virus-dependent patterns of myeloid, astrocyte-associated, complement, and lymphocyte responses across brain regions. Together, these findings demonstrate how viral genetic background and its modulation of host antiviral responses shape divergent neuroimmune states in which viral accumulation, antiviral immunity, and CNS immune activation are differentially coordinated.

papers.title: Identification of two novel lipoteichoic acid synthases essential for viability in Clostridioides difficile.
papers.abstract: Lipoteichoic acids (LTAs) are major components of the Gram-positive bacterial cell envelope that contribute to cell morphology, division, and resistance to antimicrobial stress. Clostridioides difficile produces a type V LTA composed of repeating GlcNAc-GlcNAc-glyceric acid subunits anchored to the membrane by a glycolipid. Here, we identify two previously uncharacterized enzymes involved in C. difficile LTA synthesis: LtaB, which is required for LTA production and cell envelope integrity, and LtaA, which influences apparent LTA polymer length and partially compensates for reduced LtaB activity. Loss of LtaB causes growth and morphological defects, including aberrant septation and cell lysis, while LtaB depletion in the absence of LtaA is lethal. LtaA and LtaB contain two distinct domains: an LTA synthase-like domain and a glycosyltransferase (GT) C-like domain. Site-directed mutagenesis of conserved residues shows that the GT-C-like domain of LtaB is critical for both LTA synthesis and viability, whereas mutations in the LTA synthase-like domain have little effect on viability and only modest effects on LTA chain length. Production of several LtaB homologs from related species restored viability and, in some cases, LTA synthesis when a C. difficile {Delta}ltaA mutant was depleted of LtaB. These findings establish LtaA and LtaB as distinct but functionally overlapping enzymes required for type V LTA synthesis in C. difficile.

papers.title: maoP impacts biofilm formation via csgD in Salmonella Typhimurium
papers.abstract: Biofilm formation is a key process in the life cycle of most bacteria and involves the formation of multicellular aggregates, frequently attached to a surface. Despite extensive research into the complex regulatory pathways controlling this process, many aspects are not fully understood. Originally named for its role in chromosomal organisation, MaoP has previously been shown to have an important impact on biofilm formation in Escherichia coli and Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium. Here we continued to explore how MaoP impacts biofilm formation in S. Typhimurium 14028S. We show that deletion of maoP significantly reduces biofilm formation through reduced production of the biofilm matrix components curli and cellulose, and that this is associated with a reduction in transcript abundance of the central biofilm regulator csgD. Comparison of the transcriptomes of WT and maoP deletion strain biofilms confirmed the substantial impact of MaoP on csgD and its regulon. To further explore how MaoP impacts biofilm formation we conducted a biofilm evolution experiment to select for suppressor mutants that had restored curli production in a {Delta}maoP background. Sequencing of these mutants identified single nucleotide polymorphisms upstream of csgD that increased csgD transcript abundance and recovered biofilm formation to wild-type levels. In conclusion, our findings suggest a pathway where MaoP is involved in the regulation of biofilm formation through the control of the central biofilm regulator CsgD.

papers.title: Fungal abundance and community composition associations with environmental and operational factors within and between manufacturing facilities.
papers.abstract: Fungal communities in manufacturing environments remain understudied despite their potential implications for product quality and occupational health. Surface swabs collected from 19 footwear factories in Vietnam between 2023 and 2025 were used to assess culturable fungal counts, genus-level diversity and community composition. Associations with operational factors and environmental conditions, including temperature, relative humidity (RH), CO2 and PM10, were examined by separating environmental variation into within-factory and between-factory components. Fungal counts were associated with both operational and environmental factors, with object type showing the strongest operational association. Higher PM10 tended to be associated with lower surface fungal counts within factories, while factories with higher average CO2 also showed lower counts. Alternaria and Neurospora were positively associated with within-factory RH, and Aspergillus showed a negative between-factory association with CO2. Community composition varied most strongly among factories, while environmental associations were limited to the combined effects of between-factory conditions at the community level. Overall, environmental indicators showed clearer associations with culturable fungal burden and individual genera than with overall community composition, indicating that fungal counts and community structure capture distinct aspects of contamination in manufacturing environments.

papers.title: The ACDC domains of AP2-O3 and FD3 contribute to protein interactions and ookinete development
papers.abstract: The Apicomplexan AP2 (ApiAP2) family of transcription factors are key regulators of Plasmodium spp. parasite development. In addition to containing AP2 DNA-binding domains, nine ApiAP2 proteins also encode an apicomplexan-specific ACDC domain whose function remains largely unknown. Here, we dissect the biological role of the ACDC domain from two female-specific regulators, AP2-O3 and FD3, using the rodent malaria model Plasmodium yoelii and the human malaria parasite P. falciparum. In Plasmodium yoelii, deletion of the ACDC domain preserved AP2-O3 and FD3 protein presence and nuclear localization without significantly affecting asexual growth or gametocyte production. However, deletion of these domains impaired the gametocyte-to-ookinete transition, reducing ookinete conversion efficiency. Proteomic and biochemical studies indicate that the AP2-O3 ACDC domain interacts with FD3, while the FD3 ACDC domain preferentially associates with full-length FD3. Transcriptomic data showed that over 80% of transcripts that increased after FD3 ACDC deletion were also higher following AP2-O3 loss, with female gametocyte marker expression largely unchanged. In Plasmodium falciparum, removing the FD3 ACDC domain did not affect female lineage-specific expression of FD3, nuclear localization of FD3, or the asexual growth and gametocyte maturation of parasites. Leveraging the high sequence conservation of ACDC domains across the Plasmodium genus, we conducted structure-based virtual screening of 283 compounds targeting the predicted PfAP2-O3 and PfFD3 ACDC interaction interface. Seven compounds ranked among the top candidate inhibitors for both domains, and the highest-priority ligand for each domain was further evaluated by molecular dynamics simulations. Collectively, our findings support a role for ACDC domains in ApiAP2 protein interactions and identify candidate compounds for future experimental evaluation as potential transmission-blocking leads.

papers.title: Chemolithoautotrophic acidophile phenotyping by measuring metabolic byproduct formation in microplates
papers.abstract: Chemolithoautotrophic acidophiles can support several low-pH biotechnologies, but their phenotyping remains limited by throughput and inconsistent methods. This study used an assay to monitor metabolic byproduct formation using absorbance indicators in static, oxic cultures in 96-well microplates. In abiotic experiments, ferric iron and/or pH measurements from 51 microplates containing simulant solutions span total iron concentrations of 0-1 M, pH 0.3-7.0, and incubation temperatures of 4-75 {degrees}C. Of these, 30 microplates tested different UV-transparency and gas-permeable membrane configurations. Another 12 microplates tested indicator compatibility with growth media containing ferrous iron and (in)soluble sulfur substrates. Biological experiments measured 438 microplates containing Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans ATCC 23270, Acidithiobacillus thiooxidans ATCC 19377, or Leptospirillum ferriphilum DSM 14647 with chemical additives across 1,400 concentration conditions, yielding 142,038 time-course points, including abiotic controls. Measurements of apparent substrate oxidation and/or growth from 96 culture tubes and 99 shake flasks provide context for microplate observations. The miniaturized assay and this dataset may be useful for microbiology, (critical-mineral) biotechnology development, and synthetic biology.

papers.title: Homologs of the Major Vault Protein defend bacteria against ribotoxins
papers.abstract: Bacteria use sophisticated mechanisms to defend themselves against antibiotics and bacteriophages, yet how they combat toxins deployed during interbacterial competition remains poorly understood. Bacteria use type VI secretion, bacteriocins, and contact dependent inhibition systems to deliver antibacterial toxins that inhibit growth by antagonizing essential processes. Here, we discover that Pseudomonas aeruginosa uses homologs of the eukaryotic major vault protein and a tRNA-like noncoding RNA to defend against RNA-damaging ribotoxins. Using an engineered pyocin delivery system, we showed that P. aeruginosa sensed ribotoxin damage and activated transcription of an RNA repair operon, which included band7, a homolog of the major vault protein. Genetic analyses demonstrated that band7-expressing bacteria were significantly more protected against growth inhibition by a ribotoxin that cleaved the anticodon loop of specific tRNA. Band7 was necessary but not sufficient, and defense also required a non-coding band7 RNA (bRNA). bRNA was cleaved by the ribotoxin, suggesting a mechanism for specificity and defense. Bioinformatic analyses revealed that band7 and candidate bRNA are widely distributed within RNA repair systems across diverse bacteria. Our data suggest that bacteria use structures related to the eukaryotic vault complex to respond to RNA damage thereby providing a hypothesis for the function of the enigmatic human vault.

papers.title: Hyphal differentiation and cell wall remodeling in Trametes versicolor underlie a layered architecture in pure mycelium materials
papers.abstract: Background: Pure mycelium materials grown at the air-liquid interface are promising leather alternatives, yet they are generally treated as homogeneous sheets of fungal biomass. Because basidiomycetes differentiate their hyphae into generative, skeletal and ligative cell types, the properties of such materials may instead arise from an internal tissue organisation. In this study, cell types produced by the trimitic white-rot fungus Trametes versicolor during Liquid State Surface Fermentation were characterized and the impact of their spatial organisation, mechanics and cell wall composition on the resulting material was analysed. Results: Optic and electron microscopy revealed the mats are not homogeneous but consist of two layers: a dense bottom layer of thin-walled generative hyphae in contact with the liquid medium, and a looser, air-exposed top layer made of thick-walled skeletal hyphae. Both layers had comparable hyphal diameters (2.43 {+/-} 0.42 and 2.33 {+/-} 0.50 {micro}m), but the skeletal hyphae in the mat were roughly half the diameter of their fruiting-body counterparts (5.10 {+/-} 1.05 {micro}m). Untreated mats stress-strain curves displayed sequential failure: brittle fracture of the generative bottom layer followed by ductile failure of the skeletal layer. The two faces also differed in wettability, the top being hydrophobic and highly adhesive and the bottom hydrophilic. Solid-state NMR showed extensive rigid cell wall remodelling between the two cell types: alpha-1,3-glucan accounted for about one third of the rigid polysaccharides in the generative layer but was undetectable in the skeletal layer, which contained approximately 74% beta-1,3-glucan and 26% chitin and was overall more rigid and more lipid-rich. Conclusions: These results show that Trametes versicolor differentiates into a very specific type of skeletal hyphae in liquid state surface fermentation, which involves remodelling of the molecular architecture of the cell wall rather than a simple thickening of it, and that the mechanical and surface behaviour of the material can be traced to that remodelling and to the cellular organisation.

papers.title: Emergence of mobile fosA3-blaCTX-M-65 with mcr-1.1 and tet(X4) on conjugative plasmids in avian pathogenic Escherichia coli from industrial poultry in Pakistan
papers.abstract: The emergence of plasmid-mediated resistance to critically important antimicrobials poses a growing threat to global health. Here we report the first genomic evidence of plasmid-mediated fosA3 and blaCTX-M-65 coexisting with mcr-1.1 and tet(X4) in multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli from clinically healthy broiler chickens in Pakistan. Among 1,677 high-quality genomes collected through antimicrobial resistance surveillance in Punjab, Pakistan, three isolates recovered between 2022 and 2024 harboured all four resistance determinants. Hybrid genome assemblies showed that fosA3 and blaCTX-M-65 were co-located on IncHI2A plasmids, whereas mcr-1.1 and tet(X4) were carried on separate IncI2 and IncFIA/IncFIC plasmids, all predicted to be conjugative; in one isolate the tet(X4) contig did not circularise. The isolates belonged to sequence type 93 and exhibited resistance to fosfomycin, colistin, tigecycline and cefotaxime. Comparative genomic analysis revealed highly conserved IncHI2A plasmid backbones, with an additional integron-associated resistance region in the 2024 isolates, suggesting acquisition of accessory resistance determinants. Resistance to three last-line antimicrobial classes and a canonical virulence profile now coexist on conjugative plasmids in poultry E. coli, a combination that favours co-selection and argues for plasmid-resolved surveillance in poultry production.

papers.title: Electron Transport Chain-inhibiting fungicides increase resistance to widely used azole antifungals
papers.abstract: Rising antifungal resistance in human and crop fungal pathogens poses significant challenges. Azole-based antifungals that inhibit ergosterol biosynthesis are a key first-line treatment for human fungal infections. Importantly, azole-based ergosterol-inhibiting fungicides are also widely used in agriculture alongside electron transport chain (ETC) Complex III inhibiting compounds. However, it is unknown whether the combined use of these distinct fungicides is entirely synergistic. We find that exposure of fission yeast, Schizosaccharomyces pombe to ETC-Complex III inhibitors, prior to or simultaneously with azoles, attenuates azole efficacy by inducing mitochondrial dysfunction. Our analyses show that reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation as a result of ETC inhibition activates oxidative stress response pathways thereby decreasing azole potency. Related responses in pathogenic fungi indicate that the use of ETC inhibiting fungicides in agriculture may inadvertently promote azole resistance. We conclude that the use of specific fungicide combinations should be re-evaluated in order to preserve both their clinical and agricultural effectiveness.

papers.title: Multi-Cohort Blood Transcriptomic Meta-Analysis of Active Pulmonary Tuberculosis: Reproducibility of a 50-Gene Interferon Signature and Benchmarking of a 4-Gene Classifier
papers.abstract: Background: Most blood transcriptomic signatures for tuberculosis (TB) come from a single population or a single platform. Few have been built by meta-analysis and benchmarked against published signatures. Methods: We meta-analysed three UK blood transcriptomic datasets (two Illumina microarray, one RNA-seq; 247 samples: 87 active pulmonary TB (PTB), 160 healthy controls (HC)). GSE107991 reanalyses the Berry test set, and two discovery datasets overlap Sweeney's discovery data, so the datasets are not fully independent. Genes were retained if they replicated in all three studies (FDR 1.5, FDR < 0.01). Performance was estimated in GSE28623 (The Gambia, n = 83) and GSE56153 (Indonesia, n = 36); direction was checked in GSE34608 (Germany, n = 26) and GSE81746 (India, n = 6). A LASSO and random-forest classifier was compared with the Berry 393-gene and Sweeney 3-gene signatures. Immune composition was assessed with MCPcounter and CIBERSORTx. Results: We identified a 50-gene core signature dominated by interferon-stimulated genes. All 50 were upregulated and reached FDR < 0.05 in every dataset. ssGSEA gave an AUC of 0.830 (95% CI 0.743-0.917) in GSE28623 and 0.941 (0.868-1.000) in GSE56153. Direction agreement was 95.7% in Germany and 95.8% in India. PTB versus latent TB infection gave 0.848 (0.756-0.940). LASSO selected four genes (BATF2, ANKRD22, GBP5 and EPSTI1). The frozen classifier gave an external AUC of 0.864 (0.785-0.944). The Sweeney 3-gene score, re-tested in one of its validation cohorts, reached 0.912 and exceeded the 50-gene score (47/50 genes; Holm p = 0.0234). Berry 393-gene scoring gave 0.910 with directions reconstructed from GSE19439 (Holm p = 0.0071 versus the 50-gene score). The signed score is a reconstruction, not Berry's published score. MCPcounter showed myeloid expansion and lymphoid suppression; CIBERSORTx recovered the former but not the broader lymphoid suppression. Conclusions: The 50-gene signature was consistent across three overlapping UK discovery datasets. External evaluation was partial, comprising AUCs for 47 of the 50 genes in two cohorts and direction concordance in two smaller cohorts. This is a benchmarking study, not a claim of superiority: the Sweeney 3-gene and signed Berry scores were higher, and the 4-gene classifier did not differ significantly from Sweeney. The classifier warrants prospective validation. The Berry and Sweeney comparisons are not independent.

papers.title: Environmental heterogeneity and microbial community architecture shape N2O fluxes in intertidal coastal sediments
papers.abstract: Seagrass meadows are key ''blue carbon ecosystems'', yet their contribution to nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions remains poorly constrained. We investigated environmental and microbial descriptors of N2O fluxes in intertidal sediments of Arcachon Bay, home to Europe's largest Zostera noltii meadow. At six sites, we measured in situ N2O fluxes in adjacent bare and vegetated sediments and characterized sediment properties, N2O-cycling genes using qPCR and targeted metagenomics, and microbial co-occurrence networks. Fluxes ranged from -3.7 to 8.4 mol N2O m-2 d-1. Spatial location was the strongest descriptor of flux variation, with inner-bay sites showing higher emissions associated with environmental conditions, carbon accumulation, pH, and microbial community characteristics. Vegetation effects were comparatively small and site-dependent. Metagenomic descriptors of N2O-cycling genes were more informative than qPCR-based descriptors. Taxa associated with nirS (Thiohalophilus), nirK (Planktotalea) and nosZ1 (Roseobacter) were identified as potential contributors to N2O production or reduction, respectively. These findings indicate that spatially structured environmental conditions and microbial community characteristics better describe N2O flux variation than seagrass presence alone. Measurements across tidal and seasonal cycles are needed to establish the temporal consistency of these patterns.

papers.title: Genomic Characterization of a Typical Enteropathogenic Escherichia coli Isolate from an Egyptian Fruit Bat, Rousettus aegyptiacus from Coastal Kenya
papers.abstract: Enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (EPEC) are responsible for significant morbidity and mortality cases among young children under the age of five, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Atypical EPEC has frequently been reported from animal hosts, however, information on the occurrence and genomic characteristics of typical EPEC in wildlife reservoirs remains limited. This study characterized an Escherichia coli isolated from an Egyptian fruit bat (Rousettus aegyptiacus) sampled in coastal Kenya using whole-genome sequencing. Oral and rectal swabs were collected from 24 bats captured in Kikambala, Kilifi County, Kenya. Bacterial isolates were cultured, sequenced on the Illumina NextSeq 1000 platform, and analyzed using a bioinformatics workflow that included in silico taxonomic classification, serotyping and multilocus sequence typing, virulence gene profiling, antimicrobial resistance gene detection, plasmid identification, and core genome phylogenetic analysis. One isolate, KIKB-471-SWR-A (O128:H6; ST15625), was classified as typical EPEC. Genomic analysis confirmed the characteristic virulence architecture of typical EPEC. Despite numerous antimicrobial resistance-associated genes being detected, the isolate remained phenotypically susceptible to all antimicrobials tested. The isolate clustered within an EPEC lineage, closely associated with a human-derived EPEC strain, and genetically distinct from both commensal and laboratory E. coli reference strains. Despite no evidence of zoonotic transmission, the findings demonstrated that wildlife can harbor E. coli lineages possessing virulence determinants associated with human pathogenic EPEC strains, underscoring the importance of genomic surveillance at wildlife?human interfaces within a One Health framework to improve the understanding of ecology, evolution, and public health significance of diarrheagenic E. coli.

papers.title: Deletion of Furin Facilitates Efficient and Versatile Coronavirus Pseudotyped Particle Generation
papers.abstract: Coronaviruses bring threats to both humans and animals. To initiate successful infections, coronaviruses must first navigate entry into a host cell. Coronavirus spike-bearing pseudotyped particle systems are indispensable tools for studying coronavirus entry and evaluating neutralizing antibodies and entry inhibitors. However, pseudotyped particle titers can be low when packaged particles bear coronavirus spikes that contain the furin cleavage site, and this has been a limitation for pseudotyped particle production and applications. Here, we demonstrate that CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of furin protease in HEK293T cells significantly enhances the production of functional pseudotyped particles bearing spikes containing the furin cleavage site, including those from SARS-CoV-2, MERS-CoV, and MHV-JHM. Moreover, deletion of endogenous furin in producer cells yields an effect equivalent to deletion of the furin cleavage site, but with broader application across different spike proteins, and without virus manipulation. This work establishes a simple and effective platform to improve coronavirus pseudotyped particle systems by eliminating furin-mediated pre-activation, enabling more efficient and reliable production for downstream applications.

papers.title: Precision Fermentation Gets a New Player: Genome Assembly and Genetic Transformation of a Novel Strain, Pichia hangzhouana, for Precision Fermentation of Food Ingredients
papers.abstract: Precision fermentation leverages the metabolic pathways of microorganisms to produce valuable proteins and enzymes. Pichia hangzhouana, synonymous with Zygoascus hellenicus, is a non-conventional yeast with potential for food biotechnological applications. This study characterizes the CSIRO strain P. hangzhouana FRR5246, isolated from a tea beverage, to evaluate its suitability as a precision fermentation host for a variety of industrial, agricultural and food production applications. P. hangzhouana demonstrated robust growth across a range of carbon sources, with the highest optical density observed in media containing sucrose or sorbitol as sole carbon source. The yeast showed susceptibility to geneticin, hygromycin B, nourseothricin sulfate, and zeocin sulfate antibiotic agents. Successful genetic transformation was achieved, with the expression of a recombinant orange fluorescent protein (OFP) under the control of the native glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAP1) promoter. The secretome exhibited strong antimicrobial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, indicating the presence of potent antimicrobial compounds. In addition, whole genome sequencing of P. hangzhouana FRR5246 provided genetic tools for recombinant expression of heterologous genes, insight into the genes, genetic architecture and regulatory mechanisms underlying phenotypic qualities, as well as confirming phylogenetic classification of this strain as clustering with the Dipodascomycetes, most closely related to species Zygoascus hellenicus. P. hangzhouana FRR5246 is a promising candidate for precision fermentation of food ingredients, capable of utilizing diverse carbon sources and producing recombinant proteins. In addition, production of antimicrobial compounds further enhances the potential for biotechnological exploitation. Future work will focus on optimizing growth conditions and exploring native inducible promoters for controlled gene expression.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics and Environmental Drivers of Maize Microbiome Structure across Diverse Agroecosystems in Georgia, USA
papers.abstract: The understanding of how microbial communities differ across soils, environments, plant tissues, and developmental stages is key to the improvement of crop productivity and resilience. Here, we conducted a statewide survey of maize (Zea mays L.) microbiomes across 35 fields at 16 locations in Georgia, USA, sampling soil, rhizosphere, root interior, and stalk interior at two developmental stages (600 and 1400 growing degree days, GDD). More than 38000 ASVs were produced after amplicon sequencing of 16S rRNA genes. The phyla shown to be dominant are Proteobacteria, Actinobacteriota, Chloroflexi, Planctomycetota, and Acidobacteriota. Based on alpha and beta diversity analyses, the below-ground compartments (soil and rhizosphere) revealed higher diversity and stronger spatial structuring when compared to the above-ground sample types, whereas root and stalk interior microbiomes revealed marked shifts across growth stages. Amino acid metabolism, secondary metabolite biosynthesis, and energy-related pathways predictions (via PICRUSt2) show stage-dependent enrichment. Network analyses show persistent keystone taxa (Proteobacteria and Actinobacteriota) mediating microbial stability, coupled with an increase in modularity and connectivity as we move from early to late growth stages. Some environmental variables, such as temperature, humidity, soil potassium, and soil sodium, showed significant correlation with microbial diversity indicative of a compartment-specific environmental sensitivity. Collectively, our results show that in maize, microbial community composition, interaction, and potential functionality are both impacted by developmental stages and environmental heterogeneity. This study provides a fundamental framework for understanding the microbiome dynamics in field-grown maize across various agroecological conditions. It equally provides ecological insights relevant to microbiome-informed crop management.

papers.title: Comparative landscape of extracellular vesicles across three pathogenic trematodes identifies a key conserved miRNA cargo involved in host liver fibrosis
papers.abstract: Liver fibrosis caused by Schistosoma japonicum, Clonorchis sinensis, and Opisthorchis felineus represents a major global public health burden. Here, we systematically characterized extracellular vesicles (EVs) released by key stages of these parasites and uncovered, for the first time, a conserved repertoire of EV-derived miRNAs shared across all three species. By integrating animal models, single-cell RNA sequencing, and bioinformatic analyses, we comprehensively identified the targetome of miR-36-3p, a cross-species conserved miRNA cargo. Mechanistically, we found that miR-36-3p directly targets Atox1 in Kupffer cells, driving intracellular copper and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and thereby activating hepatic stellate cells. Strikingly, in vivo delivery of an AAV8-encoded miR-36-3p sponge markedly attenuated liver fibrosis across all three infection models. Collectively, these findings establish a conserved, parasite-derived EV miRNA cargo as a previously unrecognized driver of host liver pathology and identify it as a promising therapeutic target for preventing parasite-induced liver fibrosis.

papers.title: A small molecule inhibits Neisseria gonorrhoeae pilus formation
papers.abstract: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is becoming increasingly antimicrobial-resistant. N. gonorrhoeae requires the Type IV pilus (T4p) for pathogenesis, wherein the T4p promotes colonization through adherence to host cells and resistance to neutrophil killing. The pilus also is required for natural transformation and twitching motility. Collectively, these critical functions make the T4p an attractive drug target. Previously, we developed a high-throughput screen to identify compounds with activity against the zinc metalloprotease Mpg, which is involved in T4p biogenesis. Here, we identified a lead compound, SC144, that inhibits Mpg peptidoglycan-hydrolyzing activity in both N. gonorrhoeae and other bacteria encoding Mpg-like M23B metallopeptidase orthologs. Interestingly, SC144 targets Mpgs carboxypeptidase and endopeptidase activities. Importantly, SC144 inhibited N. gonorrhoeae colonization and prevented its survival in two primary human cell culture models of infection without toxic effects on these host cells. This work provides strong evidence that SC144 is a promising lead compound with anti-virulence activity against N. gonorrhoeae.

papers.title: Two novel plant-derived yeast species in Thailandicola (Microbotryomycetes): comparative genomics and transformation
papers.abstract: Plant tissues and surfaces are among the largest microbial habitats on Earth, and commensal yeasts are common members of these communities, where they can contribute to plant-microbe interactions including the biological control of plant diseases. Here, we describe two novel species of unpigmented, basidiomycete yeasts, in the class Microbotryomycetes from the plant phyllosphere (Thailandicola erigeronia and T. cardamina) represented by three isolates from leaves of multiple hosts. We characterize these taxa through analyses of metabolic requirements, tolerance to differences in osmolarity, pH, and temperature, and enzymatic activities. In parallel, we generate near-chromosome-scale hybrid genomes annotated with transcriptome data for these novel species and a congenic isolate. We employ whole-genome and multilocus phylogenetic approaches to infer the placement of these species within a monophyletic clade. We use comparative genomics to examine how the gene content of these yeasts differs from that of other members of the Microbotryomycetes, including an apparent proliferation of retrotransposons. We further demonstrate the genetic transformability of these taxa using Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated transformation. The description of these new species, together with high-quality genome resources and a genetic transformation protocol, establishes a foundation for experimental studies of these novel plant-derived yeasts and their interactions with hosts and other microbes.

papers.title: Detection of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium and discrimination of vanA and vanB genotypes by VITEK MS Prime MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry and machine learning
papers.abstract: Rapid identification of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) and discrimination of resistance mechanisms (VanA and VanB) are critical for appropriate antimicrobial therapy and infection control, particularly during outbreaks. Matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-time of flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS), combined with machine learning, has emerged as a promising tool for this purpose. We evaluated whether MALDI-TOF mass spectra acquired on VITEK MS PRIME, combined with machine learning, could provide this information. Spectra from 388 from clinical and rectal surveillance samples (135 vancomycin-susceptible (VSEfm), 138 vanA and 115 vanB VREfm) were processed with Clover MSDAS, and four algorithms (partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), linear and polynomial support vector machines (SVM-L and SVM-P) and random forest (RF)) were trained to discriminate VSEfm from VREfm and VanA from VanB isolates. Model performance was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation and using independent set of characterized E. faecium isolates from routine practice. Pairwise and triplet ensembles of these algorithms were also assessed. In the test set, PLS-DA was the best individual classifier for VSEfm versus VREfm (balanced accuracy, 78.9%), and the ensemble of PLS-DA and linear SVM reached 80.7%. Validation within routine isolates confirmed the models robustness, achieving 100% correct classification. Discrimination of VanA from VanB was more accurate: 93.2% with RF and up to 97.1% with ensembles. Identical sequence types were found among susceptible, VanA and VanB isolates, indicating that classification was not driven by clonal lineage. MALDI-TOF MS combined with machine learning is a promising, low-cost tool for VREfm screening and vanA/vanB differentiation.
